title: Container Apps: scale to zero, revisions and traffic splitting

videos.script: Lesson 7 ran the shop in a container group. One copy, updated in place, and nobody answering while it restarted. {{env}} Container Apps keeps the container and adds what was missing. It starts with an environment: a boundary with a network and a log destination, holding the shop and anything that runs beside it. {{scale}} Then scale rules. A rule says when to add a copy, by counting requests or the messages in a queue. With a minimum of zero, the shop costs nothing at night. The first customer in the morning pays for that, in a cold start. {{revisions}} Then revisions. Every change to what the app runs makes a new revision, and the old one stays. Two can run at once, and you will run both versions of the shop on your laptop. {{traffic}} Then traffic. Ninety percent to the old revision, ten to the new, and a label that reaches the new one directly. You will work out why ten percent of twenty requests is sometimes none. {{bicep}} None of this exists without a subscription. So you will declare it in Bicep and compile it, and read what the compiler refuses. And, more important, what it lets through.
